The North Window

The wind came down from the pass before dawn, and the shutters on the north window began their slow knocking.

Alice lit the stove and set the kettle on, because some mornings a ritual was the only instrument that still worked.

“You are up early,” Bruno said from the doorway, with snow still on his shoulders.

“The anemometer stopped at three,” Alice said. “Either the cups froze, or the wind did.”

Bruno hung his coat on the nail and studied the log book lying open on the desk.

“The wind does not stop,” Bruno said. “Not here. Not in January.”

Outside, the flag rope tapped once against the pole and then went still, as if the mountain were holding its breath.

Alice wrote the hour in the margin of the log, because a missing entry would be noticed at the spring inspection.

“Then we note it, and we note the silence too,” Alice said, and she underlined the time twice.
